- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5%.
- Model consistently underestimates the 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33); add 1–3% to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effects.
- If recent sentiment shows increasing volatility (e.g., alternating +/– 0.50+), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by reducing amplitude of swings.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to target 65–68 range as anchor.
